div.p: If you believe something on this site infringes your copyright, this page tells you who to send a notice to and what it must say. It also explains what we do when we receive one, how a member can answer a notice, and what happens to people who repeatedly infringe. The law behind it is the Digital Millennium Copyright Act, 17 U.S.C. 512.

div.p: No designated agent is registered yet. This site has not yet registered a designated agent with the U.S. Copyright Office, so no registration number is shown. You may still send a notice to the address below.
Send your notice in writing to the agent above, by post or by email. To count as a notice under 17 U.S.C. 512(c)(3), it must include all of the following:

ol.li: The physical or electronic signature of the copyright owner or of a person authorized to act for the owner.
A description of the copyrighted work you say has been infringed. If one notice covers several works, a list of them.
A description of the material you say is infringing, and enough information (for example the address of the page) for us to find it.
Your name, postal address, telephone number and email address, so we can reach you.
A statement that you believe in good faith that the use is not authorized by the copyright owner, its agent or the law.
A statement that the information in the notice is accurate and, under penalty of perjury, that you are the owner of the right that is allegedly infringed or are authorized to act for the owner.

div.p: A notice that leaves these out may not be enough for us to act on it, and we may ask you to complete it.
div.h3: What we do when we receive a valid notice
div.p: We remove the material or disable access to it, and we tell the person who posted it, who may answer with a counter-notice.
If you posted material that was removed and you believe that was a mistake, you may send the agent above a counter-notice. Under 17 U.S.C. 512(g)(3) it must include:

ol.li: A description of the material that was removed and where it appeared before it was removed.
A statement, under penalty of perjury, that you have a good-faith belief the material was removed because of a mistake or a misidentification of the material.

Your name, postal address and telephone number, and a statement that you consent to the jurisdiction of the federal district court for the district where you live (or, if you are outside the United States, any district where the service provider can be found), and that you will accept service of process from the person who sent the original notice or that person's agent.

div.p: We pass a counter-notice to the person who sent the original notice. Unless that person tells us within 10 business days that they have filed a court action against you, we restore the material no sooner than 10 and no later than 14 business days after we receive the counter-notice. These are the periods the statute sets.

Under 17 U.S.C. 512(f), a person who knowingly and materially misrepresents that material is infringing, or that it was removed by mistake, is liable for the damages that result, including costs and attorney's fees. Please do not send a notice or a counter-notice unless you mean it.
We close the accounts of people who repeatedly infringe.
This page is general information, not legal advice. See also our Terms of Service and the other notices we publish.
